title: Debugging Model Training
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of debugging model training in a PyTorch workflow.
Apply a small example of debugging model training and interpret the output.
Identify a relevant limitation, debugging check, or reproducibility concern.

content.intro: Debugging Model Training: Tests make model behavior explicit, while debugging uses a minimal failing case to isolate shape, dtype, gradient, data, or training-mode problems. Security includes artifact and dataset trust boundaries. In this lesson, use a small example to make the inputs, outputs, and boundary conditions explicit.
content.why_it_matters: A passing forward call does not prove model correctness. Small regression tests and honest documentation make changes safer and easier to review. For this lesson, focus on loss not decreasing and the evidence you can collect from a controlled example.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Test shapes, numerical tolerances, gradients, device behavior, checkpoint round trips, and one expected failure. Keep secrets out of artifacts and record privacy/provenance decisions. The source topics for this lesson are: Loss not decreasing, NaN loss or gradients, Incorrect targets and loss combinations. Keep each topic connected to a checkable input/output behavior.

content_blocks.title: Read the example
content_blocks.text: Use assertions on outputs and `torch.testing.assert_close` for approximate floating-point equality; test behavior, not just that a function ran. The example is a teaching-scale check, not evidence of a trained model score or a hardware-independent performance claim.

items.title: Loss not decreasing
items.text: Connect the quantity to the model objective and update order; track it over steps and change one training setting per experiment.

items.title: NaN loss or gradients
items.text: Identify the value being differentiated and the scalar objective; compare the resulting gradient with a tiny analytical or numerical check.

items.title: Incorrect targets and loss combinations
items.text: Connect the quantity to the model objective and update order; track it over steps and change one training setting per experiment.

items.title: Learning-rate problems
items.text: Connect this topic to the lesson workflow: Test shapes, numerical tolerances, gradients, device behavior, checkpoint round trips, and one expected failure. Keep secrets out of artifacts and record privacy/provenance decisions. Write down the expected behavior and test it on a small, inspectable input.

items.title: Data-label misalignment
items.text: Inspect one sample before batching, verify feature/label alignment, and confirm that preprocessing and split boundaries fit the intended stage.

items.title: Training/evaluation mode errors
items.text: Choose a metric that matches the task, compute it on the intended split, and inspect representative errors before interpreting one aggregate score.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save as example.py in a Python environment with a compatible PyTorch installation, then run `python example.py`. PyTorch snippets are not executed in the browser. For GPU- or package-specific snippets, install the matching supported dependencies first.

content.task: Try it yourself: Write two small tests for a tensor/model function: one checks a correct result and another checks rejection of invalid input. Record the observed result and one limitation; do not report an unrun training or performance result as measured.
task_acceptance_criteria: The experiment demonstrates at least one relevant aspect of debugging model training.
Record the expected and observed result, including shape/dtype/device information when relevant.
Explain one common failure mode, compatibility limitation, or evaluation caveat.
hints: Begin with the smallest working example for debugging model training and keep input shapes explicit.
Change only one variable at a time; compare a tensor property, a printed value, or a test assertion.
Use the linked official reference for any hardware-specific, optional-package, or version-sensitive behavior.

troubleshooting.symptom: A tensor operation raises a shape, dtype, or device mismatch.
troubleshooting.check: Print .shape, .dtype, and .device for each input. Resolve the mismatch intentionally instead of changing dimensions blindly.

troubleshooting.symptom: The example fails because an optional package or accelerator is unavailable.
troubleshooting.check: Check the installed PyTorch/package versions and device availability. Use the official installation selector and run the CPU-compatible path where appropriate.

troubleshooting.symptom: The result differs across runs or machines.
troubleshooting.check: Fix the seed where useful, record versions and inputs, and document operations that remain nondeterministic or hardware dependent.

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on assumptions instead of inspecting the data or output.
common_mistakes.why: Many ML failures come from incorrect shapes, labels, preprocessing, or execution mode rather than a syntax error.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect representative inputs and add assertions for the expected shape, dtype, range, or behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing training-time behavior with inference-time behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Dropout, normalization, gradient tracking, and optimizer updates can change how a model behaves.
common_mistakes.fix: Do not hide all exceptions or assume bitwise equality across devices and package versions.

common_mistakes.problem: Using a current or experimental API without recording its version assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Hardware support and ecosystem APIs can change independently of the core package.
common_mistakes.fix: Pin compatible dependencies, record the environment, and test after upgrades.
